rv.q: The new musical The Paparazzi at the AMT Theater by composer Al Tapper and writer Tony Sportiello is pleasant enough but considering it is a satire on tabloid journalism it ought to have taken its own advice: “And remember, if there’s no heat, there’s no fire.”
Only during his scenes does The Paparazzi suggest the scorching media critique that this musical ought to have been.
A musical about paparazzi culture delivers energy and tunes but could stand to sharpen its storytelling...

cn.t: Critics find this musical about tabloid journalism obvious and uninspired, with one calling it a mere "newsflash" of well-worn themes that fails to offer fresh insight into paparazzi culture.
